item.title: A console from 1985 learns to read the news
item.description: Engineers say the machine’s 2 kilobytes of memory hold four stories at a time, "which is plenty," one said & laughed.
item.content:encoded: Not this: it is the whole story, with tags in it.

item.title: Café owners weigh a longer headline than three lines of twenty-eight characters can possibly hold on a screen like this one
item.description:
The café — a fixture of the neighborhood — reopened.

It is short.
An item with no headline is passed over.

item.title: A summary that runs on and on
item.description: This summary is far too long for the six or seven lines that a page has left under its headline, so it has to be cut somewhere, and where it is cut it ends with three dots to say that there was more of it than the screen of a console from the nineteen eighties could show at once, which is true of most things.
